xenicibis:eswiki:4.title: Xenicibis (Función de la maza del ala)

facts.statement: The Jamaican ibis (Xenicibis xympithecus) is an extinct bird species uniquely characterized by its club-like wings.
facts.quote: The Jamaican ibis, Jamaican flightless ibis or clubbed-wing ibis (Xenicibis xympithecus) is an extinct bird species of the ibis subfamily uniquely characterized by its club-like wings.

facts.statement: The bird was initially presumed flightless based on an incomplete coracoid, but flightlessness was confirmed after a humerus was found in Swansea Cave, Jamaica.
facts.quote: At the time, it was presumed to be flightless based on the incomplete coracoid; its flightlessness was confirmed after a humerus of the same species was found in the Swansea Cave, Jamaica.

facts.statement: Fossils from locations including the Red Hills Fissure show a unique modification of the carpometacarpus that rendered the wing club-like.
facts.quote: New fossil finds from two locations, including the Red Hills Fissure, show that the bird has a unique modification of the carpometacarpus, rendering it club-like.

facts.statement: Based on a maximum femur diameter of 8.7 mm, the Jamaican ibis is estimated to have weighed about 2 kg (70 oz).
facts.quote: From its maximum femur diameter of 8.7 mm, it has been estimated that the Jamaican Ibis weighed about 2 kg (70 oz).

facts.statement: Ornithologists speculate the wings were used as weapons like a club or flail, similar to adaptations in mantis shrimps.
facts.quote: Ornithologists speculate that the wings were used as weapons, in the manner of a club or flail, similar to the adaptations found in some mantis shrimps (Stomatopoda: Gonodactyloidea) that possess a club-like distally inflated dactyl used to strike prey and other shrimps.

facts.statement: This wing adaptation seems unique among birds.
facts.quote: Among birds, this adaption seems unique.

facts.statement: The Jamaican ibis was endemic to Jamaica.
facts.quote: The Jamaican ibis was endemic to Jamaica.

facts.statement: Fossils from Cuba once claimed to belong to this genus were later identified as belonging to a limpkin.
facts.quote: Bones from Cuba claimed to be of this genus were later identified as those of a limpkin.

facts.statement: The species belongs to the order Pelecaniformes, family Threskiornithidae, and subfamily Threskiornithinae.
facts.quote: ordo: Pelecaniformes familia: Threskiornithidae subfamilia: Threskiornithinae

facts.statement: The species lived during the Holocene, from 0.0117 to 0 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Holocene to Holocene (0.0117 to 0 million years ago)

rejected.quote: It is the only species in the genus Xenicibis, and one of only two flightless ibis genera, the other being the genus Apteribis which was endemic to Hawaii's islands of Maui Nui.
